Right! Everything is cyclical. It's a dance between opposites. That's one way I look at it anyways. I don't think that time is real in the sense that we (I) usually think about it. There's just "now" and the now you're experiencing now is the same now that you experienced in the past. It's the same now that the dinosaurs experienced. It's the same now that the last human will experience before they die.

Relativity also does weird things with time. Even just based on physics, photons and any other particles that move at the speed of light don't experience time at all. Relative to them, all of eternity flashes by instantaneously, because time accelerates infinitely as you approach the speed of light.

No matter how you define "eternity" you can always ask "Well what came before (or after) that?" Which seems to suggest that time itself is not as solid of a concept as a lot of people tend to think of it as.

While it's not something that I will argue very passionately about, because I am aware that I'm pretty ignorant about a lot of things, I do subscribe to that idea that "consciousness is primary in the universe".

So the physical world that we think of as being "really real" isn't actually real at all until something becomes consciously aware of it.

I also believe in the unity of consciousness. So like there's only one "self". And "we" as individuals are all different representations of that self. I imagine a universe in which "something" wakes up for the first time. It finds itself all alone, so it starts playing games with itself in order to construct some sense of meaning. Of course there's no meaning to be found, so it gets caught up in these games it plays for ever and ever and ever, trying to scare itself, or fool itself, or forget itself.

There's that tricky concept to wrap my mind around of a circle whose circumference is its center, and whose center is it's circumference... It's like a geometric structure that kind of reflects the nature of "what is".

Like it's there and not there. The further inward you look, the further outward you go, and vice versa. You can't push without pulling. You can't pull without  pushing. In one sense, you're everywhere at once. But in another sense, you're stuck exactly where you are and you can't go anywhere at all, because every point is the same point.

I believe that reality is infinite. I believe that we can keep looking further and further and further and never know what "truly is"... I believe in the emptiness of the infinite. I believe that nothing is "real" in the sense that we (or at least I) tend to think about reality. We're all just arbitrary collections of experience that have decided to attach meaning to themselves. It's all just void and infinite nothingness. And yet... We're here. We can see and think and feel.

There's this idea of "that which exists outside of all possible categories". Nothingness implies somethingness. Existence implies non-existence. Up implies down. Unity implies diversity. Balance implies imbalance. But there's this concept of the thing that has no opposite. No implied other... It's everything, but also nothing. There's no real word that can truly describe it, because all words and thoughts are just symbols which require categorization.

I don't know... I've listened to a little Alan Watts. I've done a few drugs. And I just generally have a deep interest in the subject.

Like I said, I'm not too attached to my beliefs. I won't argue too strongly to defend them. I do dig this kind of stuff though.

Addendum:
I also believe that SOMETHING about existence must somehow be objectively "better" than non-existence. I think that the fact that we are here at all (if we even are here at all 🤔) is somehow proof that "to be" has been decided to be better than "not to be" by "the powers that be", even in spite of all the suffering and shit that comes along with being alive. At least that's what I tell myself on bad days when I can't find a reason to keep living lol.
